original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Bit decoder lever (PR1084 orthogonal-pair cost-6 terms) inside the construction family of the selected bit word: exact census of the frozen PR555/PR543 L3 plan's admissible reader sets for root F2 duals, the real gen_p3 helper inventory R(P) of those reader sets, and exact nine- and eleven-stage pricing of the resulting P(111-j) units against the selected bit c and two P104 thresholds.
scope_change_reason: The track assignment (seed 4, bit supplier: improve one circuit, frame schedule, decoder or paid profile) has only two catalogue cards, both about register models or the H2/K contract. Live overlap showed both are saturated (finite-group register censuses, R439 helper-star packages). PR1084 left an unpriced decoder lever: its P102 unit fails the nine-stage hosting wall, and nobody had checked whether the selected word's own generator can reach more than one cost-6 pair or what other stage counts would give. This answers that question with exact evidence; it is not a register-model result.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the non-binding bit supplier. It does not change kappa (the complex side binds, bit headroom 3.46%). It decides whether the orthogonal-pair decoder can add bit headroom inside the current bit construction family if a complex improvement such as P104 lands: within this family it cannot (best hostable outcome: shipped P110 at nine stages, +0.70%, below both P104 thresholds).
stop_rule: Exhaustive census of all C(18,9)=48,620 (and C(19,9)=92,378 with line 7) reader sets; real gen_p3 builds of the shipped set, all 5 j=5 and all 77 j=4 sets to receiver-search convergence; j=3/j=2 sets screened with two fixed receiver choices and a one-sweep search in order of closeness to the nine-stage wall until a 1,140 s budget (coverage recorded); pricing of every built j>=4 set at eleven stages and of the lowest-R j=2/j=3 sets at nine stages.
evidence: census.py --check: PASS_BIT_P102_ELIGIBLE_CENSUS (17,478 admissible reader sets, jmax=5, P102 unreachable); independent_census.py: 127 fields agree; price.py: positive controls reproduce PR589 at 9 and 11 stages and PR555 at 11 stages exactly; screen.py --check: own-R pricing of 82 built j>=4 sets at 11 stages (-2.778%..-0.211%, 0 reach either P104 threshold), 0/2,785 built j=2/3 sets pass the nine-stage wall; CARRIERS.json.gz: real gen_p3 builds (all asserts, decoder rows and xcheck_p pass for shipped/j>=4).
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: Claude Code (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5) orchestrated subagents that wrote census.py, price.py, screen.py and carriers.py; a separate agent re-implemented the census before reading it (independent_census.py); another adversarially reviewed the pricing and found the R-sensitivity that led to the real gen_p3 builds. The main session reran every command.

open_questions.question: Can a re-planned L3 keeper/thirds structure make an orthogonal-pair reader system eligible while keeping extra carriers low (j=5 needs R <~ 443 at eleven stages for PR1084's P104 line)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The j<=5 cap and the carrier penalty both come from the frozen PR543 plan and PR555's carrier-minimising nomination; the decoder itself allows j=9.
open_questions.first_step: Score j(P) and x(P) jointly over re-planned keeper/thirds structures, reusing census.py and carriers.py.
open_questions.blocked_by: A plan generator targeting eligibility of an orthogonal-pair system's reader lines, and gen_p3 support for punctured non-reader (dead dual) lines.

open_questions.question: Can the shipped P110 (dead line 87, cost-6 pair 66-87) be realised as a legal nine-stage word?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only hostable gain found (+0.70% bit c at R=439 with 9 slack units per replica); it changes kappa only if the complex side first rises above the bit side.
open_questions.first_step: Delete line 87's source and target registers from the PR589 word, re-derive frames, run xcheck_p.py and the nine-stage hosting audit.
open_questions.blocked_by: The asymmetric rank-6 COPY from span 87-perp to span 66-perp (PR620), its terminal frame/restoration, and the H1-H5 interface.

open_questions.question: Do the built words' own paid profiles change the own-R prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The own-R prices shift PR589's profile by (R-439) average helper climb patterns, a premise.
open_questions.first_step: Rebuild the j>=4 words from CARRIERS.json.gz receivers, replay their paid profiles, transplant and price.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing; the margin to the nearest threshold is at least 1.5 percentage points, so no change in conclusion is expected.
